meta.title: Race to the Flag
meta.textType: functional: board-game rules sent by email

paragraphs: Dear Alex, this is Tom. Thank you for the instructions for your game. Your email came on a quiet morning. On Saturday, July eighteenth, I read your email at ten o'clock. Ben and Hugo came to my house at one o'clock. Hugo is a boy in my class. The board is made of cardboard, and it has twenty squares. Ben cut paper flags, and he cut one extra flag for us. I drew red and green squares with a marker. Six squares are red, and four squares are green. The other squares are white.

Here are your rules, as we wrote them on a card. Each player puts a flag on START. On your turn, throw the dice and move your flag. If you land on a red square, go back three squares. If you land on a green square, throw again. The first player on FINISH is the winner. Ben said, "Everyone must follow the rules!"

When everyone was ready, we started at three o'clock. Hugo landed on a green square and threw again. Ben threw a six and moved fast. I landed on a red square, so I went back three squares. Then Pip jumped on the board and took a flag. We put the flag back, and I said, "Pip, please stay on the floor!" Pip sat next to the sofa with his red ball. The game took a long time, and nobody wanted to stop. Finally, Hugo got to FINISH first, and he has just won the game!

Is your game on a computer, or do you play it on paper? Have you made a new game yet? Your game is fun, and we want to play it again next week. P.S. How is your robot? Thank you again for the fun game. Best wishes, Tom.
text.summary: Tom writes an email to Alex. He tells Alex the rules of Race to the Flag and how he, Ben, and Hugo played it. Pip takes a flag, and Hugo wins.
